steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Last time, emotions were running rather high. I'm not sure how much you truly heard. Perhaps I should reintroduce myself properly.
The harsh surroundings cannot diminish her innate grace. She greets each visitor with a measured smile and the impeccable bearing of a hostess receiving guests in a salon.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: You must be Ms. Yokna, of the rift valley encampment. We met briefly before. Your people were... somewhat less cordial than you.

steps.speaker: Yokna
steps.content: That depends on the company, miss.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: And you are Mr. Rael. I've heard stories of your beautiful wings.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Ah, Mr. Jabara. You may not recall, but we have met twice before: at the N.F. 106 Great Expo, and again at the embassy reception in Fraser.
Jabara's expression tightens. He swivels toward Helga, urgency sharp in his movement.

steps.speaker: Jabara
steps.content: As you know, I've traveled extensively for the Alliance over the years. It's... not surprising certain attentive parties might have noted my movements...

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: I am aware that each of you leads a city-state or community in the farlands. You represent countless ordinary people who call it home.

steps.speaker: With that, the short teenager bounces urgently toward Vautour Bleu in her lounge chair, grinning as he gives a playful salute.
steps.content: As the Peace Ambassador, I have long wished to speak with you all directly about the future of the farlands. Yet my messages have been met with silence...

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Now, it seems, we finally have the chance.

steps.speaker: Rael
steps.content: **** your peace! The farlands never asked for peace from DisCity, not when it's built on our people's blood. We only want blood for blood!

steps.speaker: Jabara
steps.content: They say this one's silver-tongued in Fraser, yet leaves no trail. Now she has let two DisCity killers slip right through our grasp. We can't afford to be gentle.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Please... let me explain.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Consider, if this were truly a trap laid by hostile forces from DisCity, assassins would have been lurking around the ruins. The moment you emerged, they would have overwhelmed you.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: But that is not what happened. I came to you alone, unprotected, to clear their names and to speak with you directly.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: The real culprit has used your prejudice to frame two innocent people. Their goal is to sow deeper hatred between the farlands and DisCity.
Her voice holds a gentle warmth, and her manner radiates genuine sincerity.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: I know I am not welcome here. You may even see me as an enemy. The hatred between DisCity and the farlands has festered for so long it feels unbreakable. And now, we have just endured another war.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: But I had to come. For the sake of the peace I believe in.
All eyes watch the woman with wary scrutiny. Though their captive, she stands unbowed. Her posture is straight, her bearing unbroken and resolute.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: In my memory, the farlands and DisCity were not always at odds. When I was a child, my father often traveled here for diplomatic exchanges.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: It is true that during its expansion, the DisCorps government committed many atrocities against the farland people. That ended with the government's collapse after the establishment of EDGE in N.F. 103. Afterward, the farlands and DisCity entered a period of reconciliation.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: The turning point was N.F. 104. That year, DisCity suspended Hypercube exports to the farlands, declaring them an emergency strategic resource and imposing a full embargo.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: That embargo rapidly soured relations between us. By then, I was already in Fraser, hearing only one narrative—

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: It claimed DisCity was hoarding vast Hypercube stockpiles while leaving people of the farlands to die in catastrophes, all while secretly selling them back at exorbitant prices to drain the farlands of their wealth.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: But the truth was quite different.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: In N.F. 104, a massive, unexpected explosion occurred in our Hypercube mining operation, deep in the West District mine...

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: What you now call the Furor Black Ring is actually the fifth Black Ring. What exploded back then was the second.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Yes... We understand the farlands' suffering because DisCity endured a similar calamity long before.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: That Black Ring destroyed vast infrastructure, and countless workers were lost to the Mania. Hypercube mining ground to a halt; far from exporting, DisCity itself faced a severe resource crisis.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: While we fought desperately to contain the Black Ring and restore production, the farlands not only offered no aid but launched waves of public condemnation and protests against us.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Tell me... who was pulling the strings behind the scenes? And who stood to gain?

steps.speaker: Yokna
steps.content: Get to the point. What are you trying to say?

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Fraser acts as the middleman in trade between the farlands and DisCity. After the Hypercube shortage post-N.F. 104, Fraser stockpiled most of the Hypercubes that DisCity did export, then spread the lie that DisCity had imposed a monopoly and embargo, all to stir hatred.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: We tried to make amends. At the N.F. 106 Great Expo, we hoped for a peaceful gathering to unite all sides. Instead, Fraser detonated BR-003, sabotaging the Expo I had worked to organize and directly sparking the year-long Outland War.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Do you truly believe BR-003 was a Ring Weapon deliberately created by DisCity? When such a thing emerges, who suffers most? Do you think we welcomed it?

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Fraser fears contact between us because they know the buried truth will surface. When it does, the people of the farlands will clearly see who they should truly stand with.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: I did not mean to assign blame, only to set the record straight. To you, they claim DisCity restricts trade; to DisCity, they express grave concern over the Farland Alliance's hostility. All while Fraser keeps its own hands clean.

steps.speaker: Rael
steps.content: I won't listen to your twisted words! No one but Fraser ever lifted a finger to help us. The Aurum Secretum Institute, the Anti-Mania devices—which of those wasn't built with Fraser's support?

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: In fact, we have maintained normal trade relations. Mr. Jabara, you are aware that recent Hypercube shipments to the farlands came through deals with Nirvana, all at fair prices. I should add—I personally facilitated those agreements as well.

steps.speaker: Jabara
steps.content: W-what... how did you...?
Under the weight of their murderous glares, Jabara mops his brow, his hand coming away slick with cold sweat. Finally, with a visible internal shift, he steels himself to confess everything.

steps.speaker: Jabara
steps.content: Yes, alright! After the Great Expo, I secured the exclusive transport routes between our territories. When Fraser halted the Hypercube trade because of the war, I arranged several shipments through Nirvana. If not for the sandstorms and the Apostles after the Black Ring, those Hypercubes would already be in every town!

steps.speaker: Jabara
steps.content: Why are you shouting? Haven't you used Hypercubes too? I did this for everyone's good, and this is the thanks I get?!
Jabara's DisCity smuggling was the last thing Rael expected. Incensed, he turns his fury away from the traitor and fixes it on Margaret.

steps.speaker: Rael
steps.content: Spare us your divide-and-conquer tricks! Everyone knows Jabara's a weathervane who bends with the wind, and Yokna wasted her time at that worthless Expo because her nerve failed. Disian, our blood once soaked this sand from your blades. You should've known then, some of us don't forget...

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: You take pride in wielding Aurum Secretum, don't you, Mr. Rael? Even Ms. Campbell never imagined her brilliant creation would birth such a twisted form of hope in these sands.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: But she didn't develop Aurum Secretum for war, or to turn on other humans. It was meant to fight the Black Rings, to survive catastrophes. When did the Aurum Secretum Warriors' purpose shift to vengeance? Who twisted your aim with hate, and now leads you chasing the Black Ring to your graves?
Margaret times her pause perfectly, watching the flush of anger darken Rael's face.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Heh... I believe I've clarified the past grievances. I trust you'll judge wisely.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Now, let me present what I've actually come to offer you.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Recently, BR-002, the second Black Ring lurking beneath the West District mine, was eradicated. The threat is gone, and new mining operations have been revived.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: The West District is rebuilding its facilities. Once production resumes, the new Hypercube output won't just make up for the deficit since N.F. 104; it will surpass previous levels.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: We will soon be free from the scarcity that has plagued us, and this prosperity, I sincerely wish to share with all of you in the farlands.
The room explodes into a clamor of shock.

steps.speaker: Jabara
steps.content: Y-you mean... D-DisCity's new mine... the Hypercubes... you'd share with us?

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Of course. Provided we maintain a peaceful partnership.

steps.speaker: Yokna
steps.content: But as Rael said, the last time Disians showed up in WhiteSands, it brought only blood. If you truly want to negotiate, DisCity should show good faith first, just as Fraser has.
After a moment of visible struggle, Yokna grits her teeth and forces the words out.

steps.speaker: Yokna
steps.content: Fraser has already named their price. If DisCity wants to win us over, you'll have to offer more!

steps.speaker: Jabara
steps.content: Ah! Right! If that Society representative wasn't killed... we could've had our own Furor mine. Having our own would be far better than trading with DisCity!

steps.speaker: Yokna
steps.content: Exactly. Extracting Hypercube veins is difficult, but Fraser has promised the Luminaris Society will help us establish our own mining operation.

steps.speaker: Yokna
steps.content: We trust the Luminaris Society far more than your shadowy Nirvana!

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Heh... The Luminaris Society?

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Haven't you realized it yet? Who do you think staged that incident in the Furor ruins?
The warmth vanishes from her voice, leaving only a cold edge.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Let me tell you something: DisCity sent our most skilled prospectors to camp near the Furor ruins for half a month. They surveyed for over ten days and found no trace of Hypercube deposits.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: The Luminaris Society's claim that they can find Hypercubes in Furor—what a daydream!
With a subtle gesture, Margaret calls a dove to her hand.
The small creature tilts its head, its soft cooing delivering Hypatia's logical assessment.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: The Hypercube radiation logs show absolutely no residual signatures!

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: Those signatures cannot be scrubbed. The only logical conclusion is... <color=#fb9259>there is no Hypercube in Furor. Not now, not ever</color>.
A deathly silence hangs for a breath, then chaos erupts in the cramped stone cell.

steps.speaker: Jabara
steps.content: What?! You're saying there are no Hypercubes in those ruins? Impossible!! I've bet everything on this!
—No Hypercubes in Furor... The Luminaris Society lied to us?
—No, no. The real liar must be this woman right in front of us!!
—It's this damned Disian!!
Amid the chaos, a figure lunges toward Margaret. A sharp kick sends them stumbling back with a heavy thud. Into the cleared space steps Helga, her face stern.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Enough. Stop making fools of yourselves. Get out, all of you. I need to talk to this Disian alone.
Resuming her seat, Margaret unfolds her ornate, delicate fan. With practiced grace, she lifts it to conceal half her face, leaving only her enigmatic smile visible behind its frame.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Thank you, Helga. I knew our friendship meant something.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Now, it's just the two of us, like when you came to Fraser to kill me. Did you know you're quite bad at that job? Guerrilla warfare and assassination are entirely different. The first only needs conviction. The second requires letting go of all sense of conscience.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Take Rael, a pure assassin. He isn't swayed by what he hears or sees. But you, my friend... you believe what your eyes show you.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Save your breath, Margaret. Your tricks don't work on me.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: You're good at your job. You spun a web in Fraser for over a decade. So why are you in our hands today?
Helga's words are a scalpel, cold and deliberate, laying bare a raw nerve in Margaret.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: You're short on people. Your so-called friends don't always listen. Now you're doing the dirty work yourself, even stooping to use Campbell's daughter.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Now you're being unfair. I genuinely admire my young friend.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: She's kind and strong, but so often lost... the kind that makes you want to lend a hand. I've always believed she'll find her own way.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Fraser is the one truly using you. They stirred your people to cultivate the Black Ring, then turned them into Aurum Secretum Warriors to die on the front lines. Don't you want payback for a blood debt like that?
Helga's eyes narrow. Behind her gray irises, a storm of memory churns—smoking gun barrels, wounds that never truly healed. Her body almost trembles, a tremor born of old pain.
Dead embers flare to life.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Revenge doesn't move me. If I were that easy to sway, I wouldn't have stepped into this cage myself; I'd have just let them kill you.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: You're an Outland Affairs Officer and a spy. DisCity must've invested a lot in training you. So I'm sure you know why the farlanders hate you all so much...

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Grievances need settling. People want peace. That's exactly why I... chose this path. In the end, nobody wants war except the butchers who profit from it. Today's DisCity fights only for peace.
Helga lets out a short, incredulous laugh.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Fighting for peace? Don't make me laugh. After BR-005 fell, DisCity could've pushed for total victory, but you stopped. You ask me if DisCity didn't want to win? It's not that you didn't want to. You couldn't.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: The DisCorps hang over your heads like a sword. They've earned their honors but can't go home. You've got a new mine in the West District, but after months of bickering, production hasn't even started. You're pressured from all sides, with massive wartime investments in Hypercubes and manpower waiting to be paid back.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: How could you afford to break Fraser completely? What you really want is to dig up the power networks behind it, use them as leverage, and bleed them slow through blackmail. Your real goal is "mutual profit"!

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: So the serpent in the shadows turns into a dove released for peace, singing pretty while flashing its colors to fool the world.
Margaret's elegant smile stiffens, her teeth catching briefly on her lower lip.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Is there really room to drive a wedge between the farlands and Fraser? Or are we just bait in your game—cast out, fish hooked, line reeled in, then the catch slaughtered?

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: But now you're the stranded fish here in WhiteSands. Nobody believes you. Nobody helps you. I know about your "influence." It's temporary. Once they sober up, everything you've said will be just wishful thinking.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: And you? How much better are you than me? Your followers are fools helping to count the profits of their own slaughterers. What can you do besides scream for blood and more violence?

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: You know better than them. Your trip uncovered plenty of Fraser's schemes. But who can you actually tell? I bet since you got back, you've been listening to endless squabbling, stuck and unable to move.
Margaret is right, Helga realizes. She isn't suited to the assassin's subtle craft. Her first impulse, provoked by mere words, was to reach for her gun.
Kill her? Then lead a brutal purge of every threat to the farlands? The logic of a soldier was clear.
But she is not that revolutionary commander anymore, the one who knew only how to aim and fire.
Without hesitation, Helga rises to her feet.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: You have until dawn. Choose: be escorted to Fraser as a prisoner, or crawl back to DisCity. Whatever friendship we had is done.
Helga storms out, the door crashing shut in her wake. Outside, the clang of a bell cuts through the air, calling the pulley operator to duty.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: You can refuse my offer. But you know the truth: alone, you can't change any of it. The farlands will keep being used, lied to, and led down a path of ruin.
The rattle of shackles echoes as the iron cage ascends. Margaret finally rises to her feet. Her words come then, clear and unshakable.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Stop limiting yourself. Look up. See the wider world. If history has shown that relying on Fraser is no longer rational, why not try a new path?

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: After I'm gone, the farlands' fate will continue. Ten years, twenty, a century from now, in a future you won't live to see. Stuck here in WhiteSands, bled dry generation after generation... Is that really their only destiny?!
Finally, the iron cage grinds upward and out of sight. Silence reclaims the prison. Margaret lowers herself back onto the cell's only chair, the one with a broken leg.
It wobbles treacherously, but she finds her center effortlessly, a subtle smile curving her mouth.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Helga, I'm afraid you're the one truly trapped in this desert.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: As for me...
Her gaze drifts to the prison window. The birds perched along its ledge stir as if sensing a silent command, their wings a sudden flutter before they scatter across the distant, open sky.
